sharedRules.timing:
One-minute concentration effects use the source's normal ten future caster regular-start markers in initiative or 60 elapsed seconds outside unless this card states a different exact clock. Ten minutes = 100 future caster regular-start markers or 600 elapsed seconds. Alignment Lock uses 24 elapsed hours; rank-7 Alignment Anchor uses seven elapsed days; Bind Element uses two future target regular ends / 12 elapsed seconds outside initiative. Preserve virtual/absolute deadlines through initiative changes, absence and suppression.
SPELL SHIELD EXACT CLOCK — Because Spell Shield is nonconcentration, its own one-minute deadline is explicit: in initiative, application records the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application, excluding any start already in progress or past. Preserve that fixed virtual/absolute deadline across initiative entry/exit, reorder, extra turns, absence, caster death and suppression. Caster death alone does not end Spell Shield.

spells.procedure:
Action; range 60 feet; V/S/F. NEW: replace Instantaneous protection metadata with one minute, without concentration, on one willing perceived creature with line of effect. Exact duration: in initiative record the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application, excluding a start already in progress/past; outside initiative deadline = application +60 seconds. Preserve that fixed deadline through initiative changes, extra turns, absence, caster death and suppression; caster death alone does not end this nonconcentration ward. Only one pending Spell Shield can protect a recipient across casters; a successful replacement ends the prior one. Interpret 3rd level and Tier 3 as the triggering spell’s actual generating rank 0–3. Caster level, discounted RP price and target class do not determine eligibility. After ordinary interruption and before any original attack, save or payload resolution, the recipient may spend its Reaction to reflect a hostile pending spell whose only selected creature target is that recipient. The reflected path originates at the protected recipient and ends at the original caster, who must fit the original spell’s creature-type, willingness, range and line-of-effect requirements measured from that return origin. Hidden eligibility is adjudicated without disclosing protected information. Revalidate, then spend the Reaction and consume the shield. Redirect the one payload, retaining the original caster’s ownership, statistics, costs, concentration and causal identity. Resolve its normal attack or save against that caster, with no automatic self-hit or duplicate roll against the former target. Areas, multiple targets, nonspells, copies and already reflected packets are ineligible. A declined or ineligible event leaves the shield available until its original deadline. No legal return target means no reflection. Suppression disables triggering while its timer continues. It cannot reflect its own creation or initiate another reflection/copy chain.

CURRENT INTERFACE — Spell Shield is pure redirection of the already-pending original spell payload. Spell Shield itself creates no replacement damage root and does not advance the original spell's damage-root creation checkpoint. The original cast ID, generating rank, caster ownership, attack/save statistics, concentration owner and source costs remain unchanged. If the original spell already created a damage root before the reflection window, preserve that root and its existing `nullNonlethal` flag. If it has not yet created a root, create that root only at the original spell's ordinary checkpoint under the original caster/dealer, and evaluate that dealer's actual Veil state at that checkpoint. Descendant damage inherits its real parent-root flag under the accepted Null rules. The protected recipient is only the return origin for range/line-of-effect revalidation. If the returned spell creates an ongoing target branch or delayed rider, that branch/rider is attached to the original caster as its new recipient while retaining the original spell/caster identity. Reflection itself creates no root. A Veiled reflector therefore supplies no Null flag merely by reflecting, and the reflector's later Veil changes are irrelevant to the original spell's dealer checkpoint. Non-damaging spells such as Charm Person create no damage root at all. The packet cannot trigger Spell Shield again and cannot be copied/reflected recursively.
spells.newChoices: NEW: one-minute, one-use Reaction protection; rank 0–3 translation; return origin at the protected recipient. These explicitly resolve the Action/Instantaneous and level/Tier conflicts.
historicalWorkedCases: A rank-3 spell with one hostile creature target can return to its caster if the return target and path are legal. A rank-4 spell remains ineligible even when discounted to 3 RP.
Two protected creatures cannot bounce one spell indefinitely: the first redirected packet is already reflected and cannot trigger another shield.

spells.procedure: Action; range 60 feet; V/S/F. NEW: create a fixed 60-foot-radius sphere centered on a perceived point within range and line of effect, with concentration up to one minute. It prevents an actual teleportation or planar-transition transaction when any transported body’s origin or destination footprint intersects the area. Cargo travels with its actual body; an object transported independently uses its own endpoints. Do not test an imaginary path between two outside endpoints. Ordinary travel through the area remains possible. The rule applies to willing, hostile and self transport using established location records; it creates no destination or plane. A portal can remain present, but transit using a blocked endpoint cannot complete. A known obstruction fails preflight before payment; hidden obstruction or a field established after commitment can defeat a paid transit, leaving the entire transaction at its origin. Atomic group travel fails together, without splitting bodies or inventory. Ending or suppressing the field allows future otherwise legal transactions but does not retry or refund past attempts. The field does not suppress summons, images, mundane movement, physical forced displacement, spells generally, or effects merely because they once crossed space. There is no save or physical cage. An explicit source exception can bypass only the prevention it actually names.

spells.procedure: Action; range 60 feet; V/S/F; concentration up to one minute. NEW: create a visible nonphysical warding plane up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high and 1 foot thick on supported ground. Every point must be within range and line of effect when created. Its thickness cannot overlap an occupied body or forcibly relocate one. Only an actual active Corrupted condition, or a source record explicitly granting equivalent mechanical eligibility, makes a creature affected. Appearance, ancestry, faction, alignment, spell tags and unrelated disease do not establish that predicate. Suppressed eligibility does not qualify while suppressed. The plane blocks affected creatures’ voluntary or forced physical crossing, including carriage, stopping that movement at the boundary. A teleport destination overlapping its thickness is blocked; a fitting destination beyond it does not cross a physical path and is allowed unless another rule prevents transport. It supplies no support against unsupported Falling; such falling can cross with the same contact damage and continues normally. The first attempted physical crossing or blocked destination contact per creature per numbered round deals 2d6 radiant, with a CON save for half rounded down; passing does not bypass the barrier. Across overlapping barriers use the earliest eligible active application for that event and one spell-family contact packet per creature per round. Exposure is spent even if defenses prevent all damage. Outside initiative use consecutive six-second intervals anchored to the first contact, preserving the open interval on entering initiative. A simultaneous group contact shares one damage roll, with separate saves and defenses. Nonmatching creatures, objects and attacks pass. There is no sight obstruction, cover, universal physical wall, diagnostic report or harvestable substance. Going around an edge remains possible; standing near the wall adds no tick. The caster is affected if eligible.

spells.procedure:
Action; range 60 feet; V/S/F. One perceived creature with line of effect makes a CHA save. NEW: a willing creature can elect failure before the roll. Success causes no application; failure establishes a nonconcentration lock lasting 24 elapsed hours. Record each currently defined effective canonical alignment axis; undefined axes remain undefined and unprotected. While operative, the lock prevents a recorded effective value from being replaced by a different one. It neither reveals values nor compels conduct. Underlying progression, Corrupted and other independent records continue to change and remain recorded, but a locked axis exposes its fixed value to mechanical alignment queries until the lock ends. Display-only masks retain their own rules and do not become actual state changes. NEW: use the earliest active eligible lock for each axis; later conflicting applications retain their own snapshots and deadlines but are suppressed for that axis. Ending exposes the current underlying state without restoring an old baseline or erasing another source’s record. Suppression retains the clock and can expose underlying changes without replaying them when the lock resumes. A prevented transition does not refund a paid cost or queue a later free attempt. Explicit absolute-source exceptions and information protections retain their scope. This grants no moral judgment, oath override or personality restriction.

CURRENT INTERFACE — NEW scoped exception `AC4-ALIGN-01` for Alignment Lock/Alignment Anchor versus reviewed Alignment Purge/Suggestion. A Lock/Anchor application freezes only the effective defined axis value it actually snapshots; it does not delete, prevent creation of, pause, refund, or rewrite an underlying Alignment Suggestion, Alignment Purge, or independent lawful alignment record. For effective-alignment reads on a locked axis, evaluate the ordinary underlying history and reviewed Suggestion/Purge interaction (including AP-AS-01) first, then apply the active Lock/Anchor snapshot last. Thus a Purge or Suggestion cast after a lock can establish its own live record and pay/keep its own costs and clock, but cannot change the locked effective axis while that lock remains active. When a new Suggestion computes its target baseline, exclude prior Suggestion overlays and Purge overlays as AP-AS-01 already requires, and additionally exclude AC4 Lock/Anchor overlays on the target so the lock cannot become a ratchet staircase. A Purge on the Suggestion caster still affects that caster's own effective orientation normally. If Lock/Anchor is applied while Purge or Suggestion is already effective, it snapshots the currently effective defined value; later ending/suppression of the lower overlay does not alter that snapshot. When Lock/Anchor ends or is inactive because a zone was exited/suppressed, the then-live lower lawful result becomes effective immediately with its original deadline/history; no old snapshot is restored and no missed application replays. Undefined axes are never fabricated.
